text:
maria: Quick proposal — consolidate per-tile permission checks into a single preflight pass at the top of the console query pipeline. Current problem: we do perm lookups per tile/entity which spikes tail latency on heavy dashboards (~15-60ms extra).

alex: curious — how would the preflight represent permissions? bitmap? tagset?

maria: bitmap seems workable for common cases. idea: return a compact mask of allowed "routes" or tile IDs + a small allowlist for dynamic resources. store in short-lived cache keyed by (user, tenant, query-hash).

kevin: this prevents duplicate checks, 👍. concerns: cache staleness on permission changes and canary rollouts where models/variants change which might require finer granularity.

maria: agree. plan is conservative: cache TTL default 500ms and we include a fast invalidation hook when we detect permission-change events from auth service. fallback is always per-entity check if mask misses.

priya: product question — does this change visibility semantics at all? we can't risk showing something that should be hidden because of a stale cache.

maria: no semantics changes. preflight only short-circuits checks when mask proves allowed. on any ambiguity we fall back to current behavior. explicit invariant: never promote allow from cache unless verified at least once in last 5s.

sam: ops implications? memory + perf for masks?

maria: masks are tiny — 128 bits per query for most dashboards. worst-case a sparse allowlist (strings) but we only allocate those for admin tenants. CPU overhead negligible compared to repeated DB/auth calls.

kevin: what about tenant-scoped multiplexed queries? if a single query fanout spans many tenants we could compress per-tenant masks into a single header to downstream services.

maria: yep — header format we sketched: `X-Console-Access-Mask: v1;tmid=42;mask=BASE64(...)` downstream services can opt-in to fastpath. fallback path chosen if header missing or mask mismatch.

maria: pseudo-config below for reviewers:

```
console.query.access_preflight:
  enabled: true
  cache_ttl_ms: 500
  optimistic_verify_window_ms: 5000
  mask_type: "bitmap_v1"
  downstream_header: "X-Console-Access-Mask"
```

ops-bot: perf-baseline: generated synthetic dashboard load (1000 qps) — p50 latency before: 8ms, after: 5ms; p99 before: 120ms, after: 78ms (access preflight on).

alex: those numbers look promising. need a canary plan + metrics: cache_hit_rate, stale_promotions, fallback_rate, mask_size_histogram.

maria: agreed — add telemetry hooks: `console.access.preflight.hits`, `.misses`, `.stale_invalidations`, `.fallbacks`. also trace IDs when fallback occurs so we can triage.

kevin: rollout steps I suggest:
- implement preflight as opt-in flag behind `console.query.access_preflight`
- instrument all fallbacks & errors
- deploy to staging, run production-like dashboard replay, measure 
- canary 1% in production with tight SLO watch
- push to 10%/50%/100% if stable

priya: product asks for a checklist item — add end-to-end test that flips perms for a tenant and asserts immediate visibility change within 2s (invalidate path verified).

maria: noted. I'll draft RFC follow-up with config, header spec, and metrics + the invalidation contract (webhook topic name: `auth.permission.change`).

sam: one more ops note — watch memory churn on our query workers; if masks are many and short TTL, GC pressure could spike. add a pooled slab or LRU with size cap.

maria: good call. we'll implement an LRU bounded cache and expose `cache_size_bytes` and `evictions`.

alex: who wants to own the implementation? I can take the server-side preflight and header plumbing. maria can own the cache/invalidation details and tests. sam will monitor infra for the canary.

maria: thanks — I'll post a short RFC follow-up with links to the perf dashboard and a sample trace.

kevin: nits: make sure downstream services that consume the header validate a signature or HMAC to avoid spoofing in multi-tenant proxies.

maria: yup — will include HMAC header option `X-Console-Access-Mask-Sig` in the spec.

priya: sounds good. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: schedule a canary run in 48h if RFC doc is ready. created ticket CONSOLE-7234.

maria: thanks — linking ticket in the RFC. anyone object to me creating the PR for the RFC tonight?

alex: go for it.

kevin: go ahead.

sam: 👍

maria: thanks all — will follow up with concrete PR + test matrix.
